(ס"ק א) אסור כו' דב"ה היה אסור כו' דאז כשהודלקו נעשו נר שמן ופתילה בסיס לשלהב' שהוא דבר אסור:
אם יש אימת כו' ש"ג פ' כל הכלים. ומקורו הא דאמרי' דף מ"ה ע"א דפריך אהא דאמרי' דרב כר"י ס"ל דאית ליה מוקצה והא בעי ר"כ ור"א מרב מהו לטלטל נר חנוכה מקמי חברי בשבתא לאחר שכבה. דאומות חברי גזרו שלא יהיה נר בשום בית כ"א בבית ע"ז שלהם או גזרו שמד שלא ידליקו נ"ח והתירו רב. אלמא רב כר"ש ס"ל ומשני לעולם כר"י ס"ל ושעת הדחק שאני דהא א"ל ר"כ כו' ומזה הוכיח בש"ג אע"ג דקי"ל בנר שכבה כר"י דאסור בטלטול מ"מ אם הוא שעת הדחק מותר כשיש אימת נכרים כהאי עובדא דרב דבשעת הדחק סמכי' על ר"ש ועז"כ מ"א דרש"י חולק דרש"י פי' שעת הדחק סכנה משמע היכי דליכא סכנה אע"ג שהוא שעת הדחק לא הותר אך מ"ש רש"י שעת הסכנה לאו סכנה ממש דא"כ אין לך דבר שעומד בפני פקוח כפש ובמאי נסתפקו ר"כ ור"א ואפי' לכבותה מותר אלא ר"ל קרוב לסכנה וכן פי' בס' ת"ש. וע"ש מה שהשיג על מ"א בכוונות רש"י הנ"ל:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
Paragraph 1: It is forbidden, etc. For at bein hashemashos it was forbidden, etc. When they were lit, the lamp, oil, and wick became a base for the flame, which is a forbidden object.
If there is fear, etc. Shiltei HaGibborim, chapter Kol HaKelim. Its source is Shabbos 45a, where the Gemara challenges the statement that Rav follows Rabbi Yehudah, who accepts muktzeh: Rav Kahana and Rav Ashi asked Rav whether a Chanukah lamp may be moved on Shabbos, after it went out, because of the Chavrei. The Chavrei nation decreed that no lamp be kept in any home except their idolatrous temple, or decreed religious persecution against lighting Chanukah lamps, and Rav permitted moving it. This apparently shows Rav follows Rabbi Shimon. The Gemara answers that he indeed follows Rabbi Yehudah, but duress is different. Shiltei HaGibborim proves from this that although we rule like Rabbi Yehudah that an extinguished lamp may not be moved, it may be moved under duress when gentiles are feared, relying then on Rabbi Shimon. Magen Avraham writes that Rashi disagrees, since Rashi explains duress as danger, implying ordinary duress is insufficient. Yet Rashi's 'time of danger' cannot mean actual mortal danger, since nothing stands before saving life; why would Rav Kahana and Rav Ashi have questioned it, when even extinguishing would be permitted? Rather, it means a situation close to danger. Tevuos Shor explains similarly; see there for his challenge to Magen Avraham's understanding of Rashi.

magen_avraham.he:
אסור לטלטלו. דב"ה היה אסור לטלטלו כמ"ש סי' רע"ו סס"ג ומיגו דאיתקצאי לב"ה אתקצאי לכולי יומא ואם יש אימת עכו"ם מותר לטלטלו אחר שכבה (ש"ג) אבל רש"י פי' שעת הדחק סכנה משמע דבשלא במקום סכנה אסור:
מותר השמן. דבשע' שהוא דולק אסור להסתפק ממנו משום מכבה ומגו דאתקצאי לב"ה וכו' [ר"ן] וא"כ בנר של שעוה בי"ט שרי להשתמש בנותר כמ"ש סי' תקי"ד ס"ג ומיהו בגמ' איכא עוד טעם הואיל והוקצה למצותו כמ"ש סי' תרל"ח גבי נוי סכה וא"כ נר של מצוה שהודלק לשם י"ט וכבה אסור להשתמש בו תשמיש אחר כגון אם הוא משומן אסור לאכלו עמ"ש סי' רס"ג סי"ד וע' בתוס' דף מ"ב ד"ה ואין ניאותין וכו' דמשמע כדברי וכולי יומא אסור מיגו דאתקצאי לב"ה וכמ"ש סי' תרל"ח:
magen_avraham.en:
It is forbidden to move it. For at bein hashmashos it was forbidden to move it, as written in siman 276, end of seif 3; and since it was set aside at bein hashmashos, it was set aside for the entire day. If there is fear of non-Jews, it is permitted to move it after it goes out, Shiltei HaGibborim. But Rashi explained that a pressing circumstance means danger; this implies that where there is no danger it is forbidden.
The leftover oil. For while it is burning, it is forbidden to use from it because of extinguishing, and since it was set aside at bein hashmashos, etc., Ran. If so, with a wax candle on Yom Tov, it is permitted to use what remains, as written in siman 514, seif 3. However, in the Gemara there is also another reason: since it was set aside for its mitzvah, as written in siman 638 regarding sukkah decorations. If so, a mitzvah candle that was lit for the sake of Yom Tov and went out is forbidden for another use; for example, if it is made of oil, it is forbidden to eat it. See what I wrote in siman 263, seif 14. See Tosafot, folio 42, s.v. ve'ein ne'osin, etc., which implies like my words, that it is forbidden the entire day, since it was set aside at bein hashmashos, as written in siman 638.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(א) אע"פ שכבה וכו' - והיינו אפילו לא נשאר בו שמן כלל והטעם דכיון דביה"ש היה אסור בטלטול לפי שנעשה הנר והשמן והפתילה בסיס לשלהבת שהוא דבר האסור בטלטול ומיגו דאיתקצאי לביה"ש איתקצאי לכולי יומא וזהו הנקרא בגמרא מוקצה מחמת איסור דקי"ל ביה לאיסורא. אם יש אימת א"י עליו ע"י הנר [כמו שהיה בזמן האמוראים שהיתה אומה אחת שהיו מקפידין ביום חגם על ישראל שמדליקין נר באותו היום וכל כה"ג] מותר לטלטלו לאחר שכבה [ש"ג וכן הסכים בספר תו"ש ודלא כמ"א ומפמ"ג משמע שאם ירא שיכהו או שאר הפסד ממון לכו"ע שרי]:
(ב) מותר השמן שבנר - וה"ה מותר הנר העשוי מחלב ושעוה שהדליקו בו באותה שבת וכבה [אחרונים]:
(ג) לטלטלו ולהסתפק ממנו וכו' - דהואיל והוקצה בתחלת כניסת השבת דהיינו שבביה"ש כשהיה דולק היה אסור להסתפק ממנו דהמסתפק משמן שבנר חייב משום מכבה וכדלעיל ברס"י רס"ה איתקצאי לכולי יומא שלא להסתפק ממנו אף אחר שכבה וכיון שאסור ליהנות ממנו כל יום השבת ממילא אסור ג"כ לטלטלו דאינו ראוי לכלום ומלבד זה בטלטול גופא הוקצה בבין השמשות שנעשה הכל בסיס להשלהבת וכדלעיל בריש סק"א:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(א) Even though it was extinguished, etc. — meaning even if no oil remains at all; and the reason: since on bein hashemashot it was forbidden in moving, because the candle and oil and wick became a base for the flame, which is a forbidden object in moving, and from the fact that it was set aside for bein hashemashot it was set aside for the whole day — and this is called in the Gemara muktzeh machmat issur, for which we hold to forbid. If there is fear of a gentile upon him through the candle [as in the time of the Amoraim when there was one nation strict on their festival about Jews lighting a candle that day, and all such cases], it is permitted to move it after it is extinguished [Semag, and so agreed in Turei Zahav, unlike Magen Avraham and Peri Megadim — it appears that if he fears being struck or other monetary loss, for all it is permitted].

(ב) (b) The oil in the candle is permitted, and "the candle made of milk and groves that lighted it on the same Shabbat and the same flame."

(ג) To move it and use it, etc. — for since it was set aside at the beginning of Shabbat's entry — namely on bein hashemashot when it was lit it was forbidden to use it, for one who uses oil from the candle is liable for extinguishing, as above in siman 261, 265 — it was set aside for the whole day not to use it; and since it is forbidden to benefit from it all Shabbat day, it is also forbidden to move it, for it is unfit for anything. Besides this, in moving itself it was set aside on bein hashemashot when everything became a base for the flame, as above at the beginning of note 1.

turei_zahav.en: In which they lit during that Shabbos. This follows Rabbi Yehudah, who prohibits muktzeh arising from a prohibition, and not Rabbi Shimon, who permits even this. According to Rabbi Shimon, the prohibition applies only while the lamp is still burning. Levush writes in a responsum printed here: ‘Regarding complete set-aside, such as a lamp lit during that Shabbos, Rabbi Shimon agrees that it is prohibited.’ This is certainly an error. Rabbi Shimon agrees only while it is burning, as stated explicitly in the chapter Kirah: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan that according to Rabbi Shimon there is no muktzeh except something comparable to the oil in a lamp while it is burning. Rashi explains that this is not because of the prohibition, but because of the mitzvah: since it was designated for its mitzvah on Shabbos, it remains set aside for the entire period during which its burning is prohibited, but no longer. This concludes his words. The Rosh, in the first chapter of Chullin, likewise writes: ‘We rule like Rabbi Shimon, who does not accept muktzeh except regarding a lamp lit during Shabbos.’ This is a textual error; it should read, ‘a lamp burning on Shabbos.’

Paragraph 2: It is permitted, etc. If so, on Yom Tov, etc., as written in siman 514. Magen Avraham there, paragraph 7, disputes Beis Yosef, who permits placing something around an unlit wax candle before lighting it so that it will go out upon reaching that point, but forbids doing so after it is lit. Magen Avraham permits placing such an impediment even after it is lit. On his view, even at bein hashemashos a wax candle on Yom Tov was not set aside due to the prohibition against consuming its fuel, since one could wrap it with something that prevents further burning, as Ran writes. Thus, a candle lit for ordinary use rather than for the Yom Tov mitzvah lacks the additional rule of being set aside for its mitzvah, and its remainder may be used. A candle lit for the Yom Tov mitzvah, however, is also set aside for its mitzvah and remains forbidden in every circumstance.
It is forbidden to eat it, but permitted to move it. Something set aside for its mitzvah is forbidden only for an act that, if done while the lamp still burned, would nullify the mitzvah. Eating the oil would nullify the lighting, so it was set aside from such use. Moving it would not nullify the mitzvah even while it burned, so it was not set aside from moving. This refers to Yom Tov; on Shabbos it is independently forbidden to move even after it goes out because it is muktzeh due to a prohibition, as Magen Avraham wrote in the preceding paragraph.
See Tosafos, etc. The Mishnah states that one may not place a vessel under a lamp on Shabbos to catch dripping oil, though it may be placed there before Shabbos; nevertheless, one may not derive benefit from the oil dripping on Shabbos. Tosafos infer from 'derive benefit' that moving it is permitted. The Mishnah chose a universally applicable ruling: consuming it is forbidden according to everyone, whereas moving it is forbidden only to Rabbi Yehudah, who holds muktzeh due to a prohibition, but not to Rabbi Shimon. Rabbi Shimon forbids only because it was set aside for its mitzvah, and moving does not nullify the mitzvah. Maharsha explains likewise. Consuming the oil while the lamp burns is forbidden because it nullifies the mitzvah. Indeed, when the Gemara says Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding oil in a lamp because it was set aside for its mitzvah, 'oil in the lamp' cannot be literal, since taking that oil is already biblically forbidden as extinguishing; it includes dripping oil, which involves no extinguishing but remains forbidden while the lamp burns because it was set aside for the mitzvah. This establishes Magen Avraham's point. Magen Avraham concludes that it is forbidden the entire day: Tosafos and the Gemara limit the rule to while it burns only according to Rabbi Shimon, who rejects migo d'iskatzai; according to us, who accept that what was set aside at bein hashemashos remains set aside, it is forbidden all day.

והמחמיר לא הפסיד. לשון תמוה הוא זה דודאי מפסיד המחמיר במה שרצונו להוציאו ומצד החומרא אינו כן ובמרדכי איתא גם כן לשון זה וכתב מו"ח ז"ל שיש כאן חסרון ב' תיבות וצ"ל והמחמיר יחמיר והמקיל לא הפסיד ותימא לי דא"כ למה כתב בס"ו דמוקצ' מחמת מיאוס מותר תיפוק ליה דמותר דה"ל כגרף של רעי אלא ודאי אף על פי דמיאוס הוא מכל מקום לא הוה כגרף של רעי:
turei_zahav.en:
His words do not appear correct. Beis Yosef explains why use of the lamp itself or its place does not permit moving it here, as it does for other utensils whose primary use is prohibited, as stated in siman 308. He writes: An ordinary utensil whose primary use is prohibited was not set aside at twilight, since it was then permitted to move it for use of the utensil itself or its place. A lamp lit at twilight, however, was then entirely prohibited to move, even for use of the lamp itself or its place. While it was burning, moving it was plainly prohibited in every manner, just as the chapter Notel teaches concerning one who places a stone on a barrel or coins on a cushion: the permitted object becomes a base for the prohibited object. It was therefore set aside for the entire day. This concludes his words. If this is the reason, there is no prohibition according to the author of Sefer HaTerumah’s position in siman 309, who maintains that an object is considered deliberately placed only when one intends it to remain there for all of Shabbos. According to our practice, we intend the lamp to remain on the table only at night and no longer, and we are particular about removing it afterward. The table therefore does not become a base for a prohibited object, as stated in siman 277, seif 3. Its law is consequently like that of something forgotten, and it was not set aside for the entire day; after it goes out, it may be moved for use of the lamp itself or its place. The authorities cited by Beis Yosef who appear to prohibit even use of the lamp itself or its place can be understood as discussing one who placed the lamp where he certainly did not intend to remove it after it went out. Accordingly, it appears to me that there is no disagreement. As Beis Yosef writes, Mordechai and Agudah permit it; they discuss a case in which he certainly intended to take it from there after the night, so it never became a base. See what I wrote regarding this in siman 309.
One who is stringent loses nothing. This expression is puzzling, for one who is stringent certainly loses the use for which he wishes to remove it, though he loses nothing on account of the stringency itself. Mordechai also uses this expression. My father-in-law, of blessed memory, wrote that two words are missing and the text should read: ‘One who is stringent should be stringent, and one who is lenient loses nothing.’ I am surprised, however: if so, why does the end of the seif state that muktzeh caused by repulsiveness is permitted? It should suffice to say that it is permitted because it is comparable to a chamber pot. Perforce, although it is repulsive, it nevertheless is not comparable to a chamber pot.

וע"ש שהביא ראיה דאם הוא מאיס כו' הלשון מגומגם. ור"ל דאם הוא של חרס דמאיס מות' להוציאו לכל אדם והוי כגרף של רעי לכל אדם. וחולק על רמ"א ואייתי ראיה מראמרי' פרק כ"ה לרבי נחמיה דס"ל אין כלי אפי' מלאכתו להיתר ניטל אלא לצורך תשמישו המיוחד לו. אם כן כלי אכילה לאחר אכיל' לדידי' היכי מטלטלינן ומשני דהוי כגרף של רעי ומותר לטלטלו משום מאיס וא"כ נר של חרס כשכבה ודאי יותר מאיס מכלי אכילה אחר אכיל' דהא מאן דא"ל מוקצ' מחמת מיאוס אסור לטלטל נר של חרס כשכבה וקערות אפי' מלוכלכים מוד' דמותר לטלטל. אפילו מונחים במקום שאינו יושב דליכא למימר דהוי כגרף של רעי וכיון דהקערות לאחר אכילה חשבינן ליה כגרף של רעי. כ"ש נר של חרס דהוי כגרף של רעי ע"ש והט"ז בס"ק ב' כ' דהא דכ' הרב"י על מאן דמתיר לטלטל הנר נצורך גופו או מקומו דלא נראה דבריו. היינו טעמא דהא ב"ה כשהיה דולק היה אסור לטלטלו אפי' לצורך גופו ומקומו. דהא נעשה בסיס לשלהבת ואסור כל השבת וכמ"ש סי' ש"ט סעיף ד' ואם כן לדעת הפוסקים דלא מיקרי מניח אלא כשדעתו שיהי' עליו כל השבת אבל כשדעתו רק למקצת השבת מקרי שוכח וכמ"ש סי' ש"ט וא"כ ה"ה הכא בנר דאין דעתו כ"א כל זמן שהוא דולק יש לו דין שוכח ומותר לטלטל לצורך גופו ומקומו ע"ש א"כ לפמ"ש מ"א בשם הב"ח בסי' רע"ו סעיף ח' במקום פסידא סמכינן על דעה ההיא דאם אין דעתו לכל השבת מיקרי שוכח אם כן במקום פסידא מותר לטלטל הנר:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
(Paragraph 3) The text should read: 'And one who is lenient, etc.,' for surely anyone who is stringent loses money or bodily benefit.
See there, where he proves that if it is repulsive, etc. The wording is difficult. He means that an earthenware lamp, which is repulsive, may be removed for anyone, like a chamber pot for anyone. He disputes Rema and proves it from Shabbos chapter Kol HaKelim: according to Rabbi Nechemiah, a utensil (even one used for permitted work) may be moved only for its designated use. How, then, could eating utensils be moved after a meal? The Gemara answers that they are like a chamber pot and may be moved because they are repulsive. An extinguished earthenware lamp is certainly more repulsive than used dishes: the authority who forbids a lamp due to repulsiveness nevertheless permits even soiled bowls, including where no one sits and they cannot literally be called a chamber pot. If used dishes are treated as a chamber pot, certainly an earthenware lamp is. Taz 2 explains Beis Yosef's rejection of permitting the lamp for use of its body or place: at bein hashemashos, while burning, it was a base for the flame and forbidden even for such needs, so it remains forbidden all Shabbos under siman 309:4. But according to the authorities who define deliberate placement only when intended for all Shabbos, while intent for part of Shabbos is like forgetting, a lamp intended to burn only temporarily has the law of something forgotten and may be moved for use of its body or place. Magen Avraham cites Bach in siman 276:8 that in a case of loss we rely on that view. Therefore, to prevent loss the lamp may be moved.

magen_avraham.he:
בשבת אסור. כיון דאתקצאי לב"ה:
ע"י לחם זה. דהוי הנר בסיס לדבר האסור ולהיתר כמ"ש ססי' ש"י וא"כ אפי' בשעה שהוא דולק היה מות' לטלטלו מ"מ צריך שיהא הלח' חשוב יות' מהשמן ועוד שאפי' הי' נותן בה דבר חשוב עדיין אין הית' זה ברור לפי שהשמן שבנר חשוב לו לעולם יותר מהדבר שנותן בו לפי שהוא צריך לו עתה בעוד שהוא דולק וא"כ אף לאח' שכבה אסור אלא שי"ל שה"ז כאלו התנה וכמ"ש ס"ד (ב"י ריב"ש) וצ"ע דהא השמן עצמו אינו אסור אלא משום דהוי בסיס להשלהבת וצ"ל דה"ק דהשלהבת הוא חשוב וז"ל רש"י דף מ"ז דבכי האי מוקצה מודה ר"ש דהכלי טפל להשלהבת עכ"ל וע"ש בתוספות כלומר דידוע דהמנורה טפל להשלהבת ועשויה לכך ולא עשוי ללחם ולכך לא מהני לחם ועמ"ש סי' רע"ז ס"ג:
magen_avraham.en:
On Shabbos it is forbidden. Since it was set aside at bein hashmashos.
By means of this bread. For the lamp becomes a base for something forbidden and something permitted, as written at the end of siman 310. If so, even while it is burning it would be permitted to move it. Nevertheless, the bread must be more significant than the oil. Furthermore, even if he placed something significant in it, this permission is still not clear, because the oil in the lamp is always more significant to him than the item he places in it, since he needs it now while it is burning. If so, even after it goes out it is forbidden. Rather, one may say that this is as though he made a condition, as written in seif 4, Beis Yosef in the name of the Rivash. This requires study, for the oil itself is forbidden only because it is a base for the flame. One must say that this is what he means: the flame is significant. This is the language of Rashi, folio 47: in such muktzeh, Rabbi Shimon concedes that the utensil is subordinate to the flame, end quote. See there in Tosafot. That is to say, it is known that the lamp is subordinate to the flame and is made for that purpose, and it is not made for the bread; therefore bread does not help. See what I wrote in siman 277, seif 3.

mishnah_berurah.he:

peri_megadim.he: והמחבר עט״ז ועיין תו״ש וח״מ דבגרף של רעי במקום שיושב שם ומיאוס באין יושב שם אפ״ה שרי לצורך גופו ומקומו עמ״א אות י״ב. ואי״ה במ״א ג׳ יבואר עוד בחדושינו שבת מ״ד א׳ כתבנו מ״ש רש״י נר של מתכות כגון של נחושת דלא בלע לא מאיס לכאורה משמע כמ״ש הש״ך בי״ד סי׳ ס״ח אות ל״ג בשם רי״ו דכלי נחושת לא בלע כ״א אור מהלך תחתיו וכ״ש כבישה דלא הא שאר מחכות בולע ע״י כבישה שוהה לפעמים השמן מעל״ע שם ולא חשיב ע״י אור מה שהפתילה דולקת בפיו רק שם עי״ד צ״ב בט״ז למ״ד ופריי שם ובשו״ת מקום שמואל ל״ד ול״ט ומסתימ׳ הפוסקים משמע רק נר חרס מאוס ושרי לצורך גופו ומקומו דוקא הא כל מיני מתכיים אם רחוצים יפה אין מאוסים (נר קרויז״ל מונח תמיד חלב בתוכו ופתילה ונפל להיתר צ״ע די״ל רק פיו בולע שם ע״י אוי והשאר קר הוא ולא אמרינן חם מקצתו חם כולו אף במתכות וא״צ לשער כ״א מעט נגד פיו ואי״ה יבואר בסדר שלישי בהנהגות או״ה) ויתר הדברים יבוארו אי״ה במ״א כאן ובסי׳ ש״ח וש״ט וש״י ושי״א בעזה״י:
peri_megadim.en: And the author of siman 17 and the author of siman 17 and the author of the book of Rei in the place where he sits there — requires study; see Magen Avraham and Eliyah Rabbah at length.

turei_zahav.he: יש מי שמתיר לטלטלו כו'. משום דהנר הוה בסיס גם לדבר ההיתר ואין לסמוך עליו שהשמן שבנר חשיב יותר עליו מן הלחם לפי שצריך לו וא"כ בטל דבר ההיתר נגד האיסור של הנר והוי בסיס לאיסור לחוד ועמ"ש בסעי' הקודם:

yad_ephraim.he: מ"א ס"ק ח' ודין התנאי כו' נראה שהציון ח' המצויין כאן הוא ט"ס שזה שכתב ודין התנאי הוא מחובר למ"ש לפני זה וכצ"ל ודחי' בידים לצורך שבת תוספות שבת דף מ"ד ודין התנאי בנוי סוכה שיעשהו קודם בה"ש כו' כצ"ל ומ"ש ודין התנאי בנוי סוכה כו' הוא מדברי הריב"ש שכתב בסי' צ"ג דלדידן דקי"ל כר"י דאמרינן מגו דאתקצי לא מהני תנאי כי היכא דלא מהני תנאי בנוי סוכה אלא באומר איני בודל כו' ובנר ע"כ בעוד שהוא דלוק אסור הלכך אפילו אחר שכבה אסור משום מגו כו' ע"ש ואפשר דהמ"א דעתו לפרש כן דברי התוספות גופא מ"ש עקר הקצאתו כו' דלכאורה הך מלתא טעמא בעי כיון דמתנה בהדיא ואומר שאינו בודל וא"כ אין מקום לקרות לוה דחי בידי' לזה בא המ"א לפרש ודין התנאי דאינו בודל אינו אלא שיעשהו קודם בה"ש אבל הכא ע"כ בה"ש הוא בודל ומה מהני אמירתו קודם בה"ש שאינו בודל אך לענ"ד התוס' לא נחתי לזה דאינהו מיירי לענין עצי סוכה גופה אם נאמר דמותר בתנאי והתם נמי ע"כ הוא בודל מהם משום סתירת אוהל אלא שכתבו לחלק דמ"מ נר גרע דלא שייך שיושב ומצפ' בה"ש שהרי עתה הוא מתחיל להקצותו ולדחותו בידים לכן לא מהני תנאי ולכן העיקר כמ"ש שבא לחלק בין תנאי דנוי סוכה וכדברי הריב"ש (וכן מורה מ"ש במ"א שלפנינו ודין התנאי כו' שאין דרך הציון שבמג"א לבא עם תיבת וכו' אחריו ולכן העיקר כמ"ש שהציון ט"ס ותיבת וכו' הוא ג"כ ט"ס וצ"ל בנוי סוכה וכמש"ל) ולפי הגרסא שלפנינו במג"א צ"ל דהמג"א מפרש דמ"ש הרמ"א ודין התנאי עיין לקמן היינו שבא ליתן טעם למה לא מהני כאן תנאי ואין זה במשמע אלא נראה שהרמ"א כ"כ להנוהגין כש"ע להתנות צריך לעשות דין התנאי כדלקמן ולולי דמסתפינא הוי אמינא שמלבד ט"ס הציון יש כאן חילוף דברים ועליונים למטה כו' וכצ"ל וי"א דלא מהני וע"ז כתב המג"א דדין התנאי היא שיעשה קודם בה"ש אבל הכא כו' אסור לטלטלו ואפילו למ"ד דמהני תנאי בסוכה כו' כצ"ל ונעשה טעות זה ע"י שהמג"א רשם על דברי ההג"ה בגליון דדין התנאי הוא שיעשה כו' וסבר המעתיק שהוא ציון לעצמו על מ"ש הרמ"א ודין התנאי וז"א אלא כמ"ש וכוונתו במ"ש ואפילו למ"ד כו' היינו דלהך מ"ד ע"כ צ"ל דאף בכה"ג שע"כ הוא בודל ממנו בה"ש מ"מ מהני תנאי שהרי שם ע"כ הוא בודל שאסור בה"ש משום סתירת אוהל לזה כתב דמ"מ שאני התם שעשוי מקודם זמן רב ובה"ש הוא יושב ומצפה כו':
yad_ephraim.en: Magen Avraham, note 8. And the law of a condition, etc. — it appears the notation 8 found here is a scribal error, for this that he wrote and the law of a condition belongs to what he wrote before; and it should read: and rejection by hand for Shabbat need — Tosafot Shabbat 44, and the law of a condition in building a sukkah that he make it before bein hashemashot, etc., as it should read; and what he wrote and the law of a condition in building a sukkah is from the Rivash, who wrote in siman 93: for us, who hold like R' Yehudah, we do not say miggo it was set aside a condition does not help, as where a condition does not help in sukkah decoration except when one says I am not detaching, etc., and with a candle — therefore while lit it is forbidden; therefore even after extinguishing it is forbidden because of miggo, see there. And perhaps Magen Avraham intended to explain Tosafot themselves — what he wrote uproots its muktzeh, etc. — for at first glance this phrase needs a reason, since he explicitly conditioned and says he is not detaching — if so there is no place to call it rejection by hand for this; therefore Magen Avraham comes to explain and the law of a condition — I am not detaching is only that he make it before bein hashemashot; but here necessarily on bein hashemashot he detaches — what does his speech before bein hashemashot help that he is not detaching? However, in my humble opinion, Tosafot did not settle on this, for they deal regarding the sukkah wood itself whether we say it is permitted through a condition, and there too it is necessarily detached from them because of tent contradiction — only they wrote to distinguish that nevertheless with a candle it is worse, for it is not applicable that one sit and wait on bein hashemashot — therefore a condition does not help; therefore the essence is as written that he comes to distinguish between a condition for sukkah decoration and per the Rivash's words (and so teaches what Magen Avraham wrote before us — and the law of a condition, etc. — for it is not the way of notation in Magen Avraham to come with the word etc. after it; therefore the essence is as written that the notation is a scribal error and the word etc. is also a scribal error and it should read in building a sukkah, as stated). And per the text before us in Magen Avraham it must be that Magen Avraham explains that what Rama wrote and the law of a condition, see below — he comes to give a reason why a condition does not help here, and this is not implied; rather it appears Rama likewise wrote for those who practice like Shulchan Aruch — one must make the law of a condition as below; and were I not afraid, I would say that besides the notation error there is here transposition of upper and lower, etc., and it should read: and one authority says a condition does not help, and on this Magen Avraham wrote the law of a condition is that he make it before bein hashemashot; but here, etc., forbidden to move, and even per the one who says a condition helps with a sukkah, etc., as it should read — and this error happened because Magen Avraham wrote on the gloss words in the margin that the law of a condition is that he make, etc., and the copyist thought it was a notation on Magen Avraham's own words — thus; but rather as stated, etc., and his intent in what he wrote and even per the one who says, etc. — namely that per that view necessarily it must be that even in such a case where necessarily he detaches from it on bein hashemashot, nevertheless a condition helps, for there it was made long before and on bein hashemashot he sits and waits, etc.

mechaber.he: אם התנה מע"ש על נר זה שיטלטלנו משיכבה מותר לטלטלו אחר שכבה: הגה וי"א דלא מהני תנאי וכן נוהגין במדינות אלו ודין התנאי ע"ל סי' תרל"ח (הגהות אשירי פ' כירה ור"י ח"ב כל בו) ונוהגין לטלטלו ע"י עכו"ם ואין בזה משום איסור אמירה לעכו"ם הואיל והמנהג כך הוי כאלו התנה עליו מתחלה ושרי כנ"ל:
mechaber.en: If while it was still day [on Friday], the person stipulated that he may move this lamp on Shabbos after it burns out, he is permitted to move it after it burns out. {Rama: Rema: There are those who say that this stipulation is of no avail, and this is our custom in these countries. The law of the stipulation is found below Siman 638. (Hagahos Ashiri; the R"iy; Kol Bo). It is customary to have a lamp carried by non-Jews and there is no issur of telling a non-Jew (to do something forbidden on the Shabbat), and the custom is such that it is as if he stipulated such from the beginning, and this is permissible as explained above.}

magen_avraham.he:
מותר לטלטלו. כיון שעשוי לכבות מהני בו תנאי [מ"מ פכ"ה] פי' אבל בשאר בסיס לדבר האסור לא מהני תנאי ודלא כמ"ש ב"י בשם הרשב"ץ ואף שבססי' תקי"ח משמע דלא מהני תנאי אפילו בסוכה רעועה היינו משום דבי"ט קי"ל כר"י אבל בשבת קי"ל כר"ש ומ"מ צ"ע דהא במוקצה מחמת איסור אפי' בשבת קי"ל כר"י עמש"ש:
י"א דלא מהני. ואפי' למ"ד דמהני תנאי בסוכה היינו משום שעשוי מקודם ועתה ב"ה יושב ומצפה אימתי תפול משא"כ הכא עיקר הקצאתו ב"ה ודחיה בידים לצורך שבת תוס' דף מ"ד:
ודין התנאי וכו'. שיעשהו קודם ב"ה אבל הכא אינו יכול לומר איני בודל כל ב"ה דהא ב"ה הוא דולק וע"כ אסור לטלטלו:
איסור אמירה לעכו"ם. ואף על גב דבסי' רע"ו ס"ג התיר לומר לעכו"ם היינו דוקא לצורך גופו שרי משום דהא איבעי ישראל הוי מטלטל ליה טלטול מן הצד אבל הכא מיירי שאינו עושה אלא לצורך הנר שלא יגנוב הנר וזה אסור אפי' בטלטול מן הצד כמ"ש סי' שי"א ס"א וס"ה ויש בו איסור אמירה:
magen_avraham.en:
It is permitted to move it. Since it is made to go out, a condition helps for it, Maggid Mishneh, chapter 25. Meaning: regarding another base for a forbidden item, a condition does not help, unlike what the Beis Yosef wrote in the name of the Rashbatz. Although at the end of siman 518 it implies that a condition does not help even with a rickety sukkah, that is because on Yom Tov we rule like Rabbi Yehudah. But on Shabbos we rule like Rabbi Shimon. Nevertheless, this requires study, for with muktzeh because of prohibition, even on Shabbos we rule like Rabbi Yehudah; see what I wrote there.
Some say that it does not help. Even according to the one who says that a condition helps with a sukkah, that is because it was made beforehand, and now, at bein hashmashos, he sits and waits for when it will fall. This is not so here, where its essential setting-aside is at bein hashmashos and it was actively rejected for the sake of Shabbos, Tosafot, folio 44.
And the law of the condition, etc. That he should make it before bein hashmashos. But here he cannot say, I am not separating myself from it for all of bein hashmashos, for at bein hashmashos it is burning, and therefore it is forbidden to move it.
The prohibition of instructing a non-Jew. Although in siman 276, seif 3, he permitted telling a non-Jew, that is specifically when it is for the need of his body, where it is permitted because if the Jew wanted, he could move it indirectly. But here he speaks where he acts only for the need of the lamp, so that the lamp not be stolen, and this is forbidden even through indirect moving, as written in siman 311, seif 1 and seif 5; and there is a prohibition of instructing a non-Jew.

rabbi_akiva_eiger.en: Magen Avraham, note 9 — there is also a prohibition of speech; at first glance even though here it deals with moving it from sun to shade, nevertheless to permit it, since he has permission to move it himself as tiltul min hatzad for his bodily need and its place, it must be that it is possible for him to move this very thing himself as tiltul min hatzad for that matter as he moves it now through a gentile; and since he can move this thing itself as tiltul min hatzad, it is permitted through a gentile in the usual manner; but to permit through a gentile for the vessel's need lest it be stolen — from the fact that he can move it himself for his bodily need and its place — we do not say this, for it is two matters; and therefore the law should be that a vessel whose melacha is for prohibition — it is forbidden to tell a gentile to move it lest it be stolen, even though he has permission himself for his bodily need and its place — unlike the view of Eshel Avraham on Magen Avraham, siman 307, note 29, who strained to say that specifically two matters — that from the fact he can move tiltul min hatzad for his bodily need and its place, it is permitted through a gentile in the usual manner lest it be stolen; but for one matter we say that since he can move it himself as tiltul min hatzad for his bodily need and its place, it is permitted through a gentile lest it be stolen; and so with a candle lit on it — for example, since he can move it itself as tiltul min hatzad for his bodily need and its place, it is permitted through a gentile in the usual manner for his bodily need and its place — or one must say the essence is that there must be possibility to move it himself for the matter for which he moves it through a gentile; and a vessel whose melacha is for prohibition is forbidden through a gentile lest it be stolen. However, accordingly it is difficult — behold here it deals with moving it for the vessel lest it be stolen — if so, what does it help that he conditioned? Nevertheless the vessel itself is a vessel whose melacha is for prohibition, as explained in Tosafot Shabbat 172, etc., s.v. deha — every candle, even if not lit, is called a vessel whose melacha is for prohibition; and for this purpose a condition does not apply. And perhaps it is proven in truth from this that we rule like the Rashba, who wrote in his novellae Shabbat 122 that a candle is not called whose melacha is for prohibition, for it does not serve a forbidden melacha but only became a base; and in responsa Tashbatz, part 1, siman 337, so too in the name of the Ramban in the name of the Raavad — perhaps here for moving through a gentile he relies on the Rashba's view, since the Jew himself may move it lest it be stolen; but regarding a Jew moving a candle on Shabbat lest it be stolen — perhaps they are not lenient like the Rashba in this, and as we say: since there are poskim that a condition helps, we rely on them for moving through a gentile; so too one may say for this matter one may rely through a gentile on the Rashba's approach.

(Paragraph 5) By means of bread, etc. Nevertheless, the bread must be significant, etc., as written below in siman 310.
It is as though he stipulated, for we see that he placed bread on it in order to move it by means of the bread.
This requires examination, for the oil itself, etc. What difference does it make that the oil is more important than the bread, when the oil itself is not muktzeh? That is, it is known, etc., and made for that purpose, etc. See what I wrote in siman 277:3. Magen Avraham writes there, paragraph 8, that if bread and a knife were on the table at bein hashemashos along with the lamp, the table is a base for both a forbidden and a permitted object. Why do we not say the flame, while burning, is nevertheless more important to him than the bread and knife? Magen Avraham distinguishes: a menorah is made for a lamp, not bread, whereas a table is made for bread just as it is made to hold the menorah. Tosafos's words cited there are precise: the Gemara had to say that lamp, oil, and wick become a base for the flame. Otherwise, the lamp would be a base both for the forbidden flame and for the permitted oil and wick, although the flame while burning is more important than the vessel. Evidently, the flame is considered more important only relative to bread, for the menorah is not made for bread; it is made for oil and wick just as for the flame, so the flame is not considered more important than they are.

In this I have room to argue — it appears from the Ran, chapter 3 of Beitzah daf 126, that their dispute between R' Yehudah and R' Shimon in muktzeh machmat mi'us is whether we say miggo it was set aside — R' Shimon holds that from the time he wishes to use this and is not concerned about its repulsiveness, its muktzeh status is removed, and we do not say miggo it was set aside, see there; and if so, all the while he does not take it to use, its muktzeh remains; and as R' Yehudah holds — an old candle forbidden even for its place, for it is unfit for anything — so too for R' Shimon they do not disagree except from the time he wishes to use it, for then its muktzeh is removed; and therefore for its place it is forbidden all the while he does not wish to use it, for its muktzeh is still upon it. Paragraph 6: It is permitted, etc. Since it is made to go out, etc. This differs from Beis Yosef's citation of Tashbetz, who holds that a stipulation is ineffective only for the object itself made muktzeh due to a prohibition, but effective where the prohibition arises solely because it became a base. Maggid Mishneh disagrees: even for a base a stipulation is generally ineffective; it works only for a lamp's base because the lamp is expected to go out.
Even with an unstable sukkah, which is expected to fall and resembles a lamp expected to go out, a stipulation is nevertheless ineffective.
Because on Yom Tov we rule like Rabbi Yehudah, etc. Since an unstable sukkah is expected to fall and a person awaits its fall, the unstated intent is like a stipulation; Rabbi Shimon therefore permits it, and an explicit stipulation works even for a sound sukkah. The same applies to a lamp under Rabbi Shimon. Rabbi Yehudah forbids an unstable sukkah despite that expectation, treating even an explicit stipulation as ineffective. Thus on Yom Tov, when we rule like Rabbi Yehudah, a stipulation is ineffective, whereas on Shabbos, when we rule like Rabbi Shimon, it is effective. Magen Avraham objects: regarding muktzeh due to a prohibition, we rule like Rabbi Yehudah even on Shabbos; without a stipulation, an extinguished lamp remains forbidden although one awaits its extinction, so a stipulation should likewise fail. See what I wrote there: a lamp is more certain to go out than an unstable sukkah is to fall, and therefore that greater expectation combined with a stipulation is effective. See siman 518.
